deal_summary: Northwind Paper ships eight 48" x 40" pallets (about 600 lb each) from their Chicago distribution center to their Atlanta branch about 40 times a month, needing a liftgate at delivery because the Atlanta location has no dock. They prefer standard, reliable transit with no temperature control and are flexible on delivery windows during business hours.

lanes.rationale: LTL is the right fit for an 8‑pallet, ~4,800‑lb shipment, and the STANDARD service level provides the reliability they value while keeping costs competitive; the liftgate accessorial is included to address the no‑dock condition at the Atlanta destination.

assumptions: The Chicago pickup will use the existing dock and forklift without any additional accessorials.
All shipments are dry freight and will not be exposed to rain during transit.
Business hours at the Atlanta branch are typical 8 am–5 pm, allowing first‑come‑first‑served deliveries.
The liftgate will be required on every delivery, as the customer indicated it’s a consistent need.
Weight per pallet is 600 lb, totaling 4,800 lb per shipment.
open_questions: Can you confirm that a liftgate is required on every single delivery to Atlanta?
Are there any specific cut‑off times or preferred delivery windows we should be aware of?
Do you have any restrictions on truck dimensions or height at the Atlanta location?
Will there ever be a need for inside delivery beyond the liftgate, such as moving pallets into the building?
Do you anticipate any seasonal spikes that could increase the monthly shipment count beyond 40?
